page_title: Archivarix Tube Search — Find Deleted YouTube Videos

sources.entry: Archivarix Tube Search: Search engine over ~1.5 billion archived YouTube videos including deleted, private, or region-blocked content. Uses LLMs to generate detailed video summaries and auto-transcribe videos without captions. Free anonymous tier; MCP server available for AI assistants.

summary.name: Archivarix Tube Search
summary.one_liner: A search engine that looks up deleted, removed, or unavailable YouTube videos in web archives such as the Wayback Machine and Common Crawl.
use_cases: Finding a deleted or removed YouTube video
Recovering titles, descriptions and view counts of vanished videos
Browsing all archived videos from a channel
Checking whether a video file survives on Archive.org
summary.what_it_does: Archivarix Tube Search lets you search by channel URL or handle, or look up a single video by URL or 11-character ID, to find archived metadata such as titles, descriptions, view counts and thumbnails. It also offers full-text search across titles, descriptions and subtitle transcripts, with support for quoted phrases, minus exclusion and OR. Subtitles can be downloaded in SRT format from YouTube caption archives and Wayback Machine snapshots. Where available, it checks whether the video file itself was preserved on Archive.org so it can be watched. The page states over 4 billion YouTube video records indexed since 2005. The listing additionally describes LLM-generated summaries, auto-transcription of videos without captions, and an MCP server for AI assistants, though these are not described on the page text itself.
notable: Searches Wayback Machine and Common Crawl for deleted YouTube video records
Downloads recovered subtitles in SRT format
Full-text search across titles, descriptions and subtitle transcripts
Listing mentions a free anonymous tier and an MCP server for AI assistants
caveats: Archived copies may be missing; video files are only available when preserved on Archive.org
Listing reports about 1.5 billion archived videos, while the page itself says over 4 billion records, so the figures differ
